why: The answer writes all three parts of the copy: a new array of the original's length, a loop over every index, and an element-by-element assignment. But it uses data2.length() where Java needs the field data2.length, so the code does not compile. This is a single slip in otherwise rule-correct code, so it is L2 with an error.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The answer creates a new array and copies each element in index order, which is the right plan. However, length() is a method call that arrays do not have, so the code fails to compile.
The answer sizes the new array from the original, which is correct. The size expression is wrong because it should be data2.length, without the parentheses.
int is used correctly as the element type and as the type of the loop index, but there is no int arithmetic to reason about.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The loop has the right initialiser, test and update, so it would visit indices 0 to n-1. The bound uses the method call length(), which arrays do not have, so the test does not compile.
